analyst_view.overall: Nottingham Forest (17th, 9 pts, above Sunderland only on goal difference) host Chelsea (8th, 16 pts) on Friday night after both lost last weekend: Forest 2-0 at Bournemouth, Chelsea 4-1 at home to Leeds to boos. Forest under Oliver Glasner have been sturdier at home (one preview notes they have not conceded more than once in a league game at the City Ground in 2026), but Nicolás Domínguez and Callum Hudson-Odoi are out, and Xaver Schlager and Neco Williams were doubts last week. Xabi Alonso's Chelsea are without Reece James and Maxence Lacroix, with Joao Pedro, Moisés Caicedo (back, off before half-time against Leeds), Jorrel Hato and Jamie Gittens all doubts. The numbers now list these absences and already take Joao Pedro's goals off Chelsea (-18.4%), so last view's small cut for him is dropped. Andy Madley referees (3.7 cards a game, already counted); neither side is in Europe, so there is no midweek rotation.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.6 goals, 1.5 for Forest and 1.1 for Chelsea. Last time I cut a little for Joao Pedro, but the numbers now count his absence themselves (-18.4% on Chelsea's goals), so that cut goes. Forest's tight home record and Chelsea's flat form point down, Chelsea's leaky defence (20 conceded in 11) points up, so I stay at 2.6.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.9 corners, 4.9 each, already adding a little for Forest's recent corner count and taking 5% off Chelsea's quieter run. Without Reece James Chelsea lose crossing from the right, but he has been out for weeks and that sits in their recent figures, so I stay at about 10.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.2 cards and already take 7.7% off for Andy Madley, who shows 3.7 a game, plus Chelsea's quieter recent run. Glasner has asked Forest to be 'more physical' in a relegation scrap, which points up, while Caicedo, Chelsea's busiest midfield fouler, is a major doubt, which points down; with those pulling against each other I stay at 4.2.

shots.text: The numbers say 26.1 shots, with Forest expected to shoot more (14.7) after 99 shots in their last six, which the numbers already count (+12.9%). If Caicedo misses out Chelsea's midfield thins and Forest could see more of the ball, but that is not confirmed and Chelsea's lack of intensity is already in their recent figures, so I stay at 26.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.6 shots on target. Forest have been shooting a lot but landing few (one on target from 17 at Bournemouth), while Chelsea hit the target fairly often, and the numbers weigh both. Joao Pedro's absence is already taken off Chelsea's goals by the numbers, and Hato, listed out, is only a doubt per Sports Mole, a small thing, so I stay at 8.6.
